title: What If Every Insect on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every insect vanished? Your fruit bowl would empty first.
Insect pollination is needed by more than 85 percent of the world's flowering plants.
Billions of dollars of fruit, vegetable and nut crops in North America alone depend on them every year.
Flowering plants supply 50 to 90 percent of the human diet, depending on the country. Animals that never eat insects would lose their food too.
Dead wood and carcasses would linger far longer, because insects, with bacteria and fungi, break down organic matter.
And this isn't far off. Surveys suggest 40 percent or more of insect species may face extinction.

description:
What if every insect vanished?
The plants we eat and the animals that eat them would unravel.
